subject: Groves et al. (2010)
object: Groves et al. (2010) reported a 38-year-old man with an inherited skin fragility disorder who had lifelong generalized trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions, particularly around the ankles. From age 37 years he experienced episodic numbness in his limbs; he also had a concomitant diagnosis of CADASIL, which the authors noted complicated interpretation of whether the neurologic symptoms were due to the DST mutation.

subject: Groves et al. (2010)
object: In a 38-year-old man with autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex, Groves et al. (2010) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation, p.Gln1124X, in the DST gene within the region encoding the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform BPAG1-e (BP230). The authors concluded that BPAG1-e pathology underlies a new form of autosomal recessive EBS.

subject: DST p.Q1124*
Groves et al. (2010)
object: Groves et al. (2010) found that the DST p.Gln1124X mutation led to loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and complete absence of skin immunostaining for BPAG1-e, with reduced labeling for plectin, beta-4 integrin, and type XVII collagen.

subject: Liu et al. (2012)
object: Liu et al. (2012) reported autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex caused by loss of BPAG1-e expression.

subject: Ganani et al. (2021)
object: Ganani et al. (2021) used whole-exome and direct sequencing to identify biallelic DST mutations in 5 patients with epidermolysis bullosa simplex from 3 families. Two of the variants had not been reported before: c.7097dupA (p.Tyr2366X) and c.7429delC (p.Leu2477Serfs*13).

Ganani et al. (2021)
object: Ganani et al. (2021) reviewed 6 previously reported cases, bringing the total number of individuals with EBS due to DST variants to 11. They noted that patients displayed distinctive phenotypes regardless of the causative variant.

subject: Ganani et al. (2021)
object: Ganani et al. (2021) stated that DST-associated EBS is transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait and is caused by mutations in DST, which encodes an epithelial isoform of dystonin.
